chapter: Washington in the 1930s: big bands, lessons, first jobs
title: Wyn Boyd teaches fundamentals and practical harmony
summary: His new fifteen-cent teacher teaches reading and chords, and Malachi is grateful to his father for the change.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Anyway, that was the first and last lesson that I had from Jack Smith. And a couple of weeks later, my father came to me and told me that there was a fellow down the street in the neighborhood that was going to give me piano lessons, which I later learned my father was paying 15 cents a lesson for. So when the proper time came, I went to this fellow. His name was Wynberry Boyd. And since then he's changed his name to Wyn Boyd -- I guess that's for pretty obvious reasons.

But I think this turned out to be another turning point. Because besides teaching me the fundamentals of the music and everything from the characters on the staff and what the time signatures meant, and of course, you always had the do-re-me-fa-sol-la-ti-do in school, and most (?)s were familiar with that... But the most significant thing I think that he taught

me was something that I later learned there weren't very many other teachers teaching at that particular time, and that was practical harmony, which meant using the chords. And he really taught me these chords, and that was when I really became very much interested. Because liking harmony as much as I did, every time I struck a chord, it just went straight to my soul, you know! I can always remember the first time I played a diminished seventh chord. I just thought that was just the most beautiful thing. Then, of course, the augmenteds and whatnot...

That turned out to be a very good thing to me, and I am always grateful to my father for having done that. I was glad that he had had the foresight to take me away from this other fellow, who was a good pianist himself, but the way he was teaching me, without the basics of any music... Because when he came in, he didn't have not a sheet of music, less more a book. He was just showing me stuff that he was doing on the keyboard, which if I had continued this, I guess it would have made quite a difference in my career.
